answer: One defense is latency triangulation: beacons on different continents send each identity unpredictable timing challenges, and only a host physically near its claimed location can answer within the tight round-trip bounds the speed of light allows. A single machine cannot pretend to be in many places at once, so every fake identity needs its own real host at a distinct location — like cutting a fresh slab of shale for each counterfeit, or setting a separate jade seal for every forged sonnet. The cost grows linearly and cannot be shared or amortized across identities.
